thread:
maria: Posted RFC for sealed catalog fragment reconciliation for on-prem packaging. Link: https://go/redwood/rfcs/sealed-catalog-frag-reconcile. TL;DR: allow partial manifests, idempotent apply by operator, and signer escrow for offline nodes. Please skim and drop quick takes.

ops-bot: RFC published by maria: https://go/redwood/rfcs/sealed-catalog-frag-reconcile (auto-post)

sanjay: quick q — how do we ensure atomic activation when fragments arrive out-of-order? can operator apply partially and still be consistent?

maria: short answer: operator buffers until checkpoint threshold and uses seq-based activation watermark. each fragment carries prev-hash and seq so we can detect holes. snippet:
```
fragment: {
  id: "m-123-4",
  seq: 4,
  prev: "m-123-3",
  size: 124MB,
  sha256: "abc...",
  sig: "MEUCIQ..."
}
```
operator holds fragments in staging and only flips activation once checkpoint sig present.

kevin: if operator crashes/restarts, do we need a durable ledger or is local disk+reconcile ok? curious about recovery semantics.

maria: durable ledger required for islanded/offline clusters. plan: write-ahead log + compact checkpoints. WAL at /var/lib/redwood/fraglog, compaction at checkpoint intervals to avoid unbounded growth.

julie: ops/security question — many clusters disallow root processes and have restricted PVCs. how does operator access keys and write logs without escalations?

maria: capability model in RFC: controller runs non-root, writes to PVC. signer private keys handled by a signer sidecar that talks to KMS-proxy (or HSM in air-gapped mode). minimal RBAC + filesystem policies. example policy line in doc: `policy: allow write: /var/lib/redwood/fraglog`.

sanjay: what about corrupt fragments or partial uploads? do we quarantine + replay from checkpoint? need clear admin flows.

maria: yes — checksum + merkle root per manifest set. corrupt fragment => quarantine + operator halts activation and emits audit event. recovery CLI: `redwoodctl fragment repair --from-checkpoint <checkpoint-id>` which will validate then replay.

kevin: perf question: large models might be split into thousands of shards/fragments. does operator scale apply/reconcile in parallel or is it strictly serial by seq?

maria: we support parallel apply within non-overlapping seq ranges; commit/activation respects global seq watermark. also streaming merge for large sets; batching window default 2s (configurable) to balance latency and throughput. RFC includes perf numbers from a local sim.

julie: :thumbsup: left inline comments on the "operator restart safety" section — mostly wording and one extra test suggestion for flaky disk scenarios.

sanjay: I'll flip a quick PoC this week to exercise WAL+restart. pinging @maria if I hit infra bits.
